entities.summary: Gashaka-Gumti National Park (GGNP) is a national park in Nigeria. It was gazetted from two game reserves in 1991 and is Nigeria's largest national park. It is located in the eastern provinces of Taraba and Adamawa to the border with Cameroon. The total area covers about 6,402 km2, much of the northern GGNP is savannah grassland, while the southern GGNP sector of the park has a rugged terrain characterized by very mountainous, steep slopes as well as deep valleys and gorges, and is home to montane forests. Gashaka Gumti National Park is a cultural heritage from Africa. Classified as Tier C (Archaeological) evidence. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gashaka Gumti National Park's montane forests and rugged terrain support unique biodiversity, with over 1,000 plant species and 700 bird species documented. The park's conservation efforts contribute to regional ecosystem preservation.
